newsitem.title: USA: Apollon says vaccine protected chimps against HIV.
newsitem.headline: Apollon says vaccine protected chimps against HIV.

text.p: Apollon Inc said Tuesday that scientists reported success in protecting two chimpanzees against HIV infection using Apollon's two-component DNA-based vaccine.

The privately held company said that one of the vaccine components contains genes encoding the envelope protein of HIV and the other contains genes encoding the core protein and several other viral proteins.
Apollon said that each chimp was injected with enough HIV to infect 250 animals.

According to the company, the single control animal was infected with HIV, and the two vaccinated ones were both protectd against infection and were free of detectable virus at 22 weeks after virus challenge.
Apollon said the study is published in the May 1997 issue of Nature Medicine.
